lesson_title: Five Animals, One River, Five Classes
hook_text: A fish, a frog, a crocodile, an eagle and an impala walk into a river. Every one is a different class.
clip_script: All five have a backbone, so they are vertebrates. But ask four questions and they split apart. What covers it? Fish: scales. Frog: wet skin. Crocodile: dry scales. Eagle: feathers. Impala: fur. How does it breathe? Fish use gills; the rest use lungs. Is it warm-blooded? Only the eagle and the impala make their own heat. How does it have babies? Fish and frogs lay soft eggs in water. Crocodiles and eagles lay shelled eggs. The impala gives birth and feeds its baby milk. Now the tricky ones. Whale? Mammal. Bat? Mammal. Penguin? Bird. Never judge by where it lives. Check the four questions.
visual_style: A whiteboard river scene with five animals; four question cards sweep across and sort them into five labelled columns; then a whale, bat and penguin jump into the right columns.
pacing: Quick river set-up, four rapid sorting rounds, three trick questions.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and classify any animal with four questions.
